walkthrough_label: STACKED CASE S1-A - diabetes medicine mix-up: low sugar, an SGLT2 inhibitor and poor long-term control, with raised BP
reason_answer: To have my gallbladder taken out.

presentation.summary: Mr Imran Siddiqui, 58, is booked for keyhole gallbladder removal. He is shaky and sweaty and says he feels hungry. Glucose 3.6. BP 174/102.

history.answer: I am here for my gallbladder, but I feel shaky and hungry.
No chest pain, no fever. Sweaty and shaky since I got up.
Type 2 diabetes for nine years; high blood pressure for six years; gallstones.
Metformin, gliclazide, dapagliflozin, amlodipine and ramipril. I took my gliclazide this morning with my usual breakfast tea but no breakfast.
No anaesthetic problems in the family.

observations.note: After the low sugar is treated: calmer, BP 160/94.

examination.finding: Slightly pale and sweaty, alert, talking normally.
Mild tenderness under the right ribs.

scores.name: NEWS2
scores.note: Heart rate 96 scores 1; NEWS2 does not detect low glucose

problems.label: Hypoglycaemia (glucose 3.6) from a sulfonylurea taken while fasting
problems.why: The scariest number (BP 172/100) is not the most urgent; the glucose of 3.6 is. Treat now, recheck, and tell the anaesthetist.
expected_actions: Ask what he took this morning
Tell the senior and the anaesthetist
Diabetes team to correct the plan

problems.label: SGLT2 inhibitor and fasting: risk of ketoacidosis even with a normal sugar
problems.why: UK 2025 consensus: omit the day before and the day of surgery; check ketones if unsure.
expected_actions: Ask when he last took it

problems.label: HbA1c 76 above the limit of 69 for planned surgery
problems.why: Optimisation is recommended before elective surgery; with a hypoglycaemic event on the day, the list is usually postponed.

problems.label: Blood pressure 174/102 (below 180/110)
problems.why: Raised but not severe; on its own it would allow surgery, with the GP reviewing afterwards.

decisions.prompt: Glucose 3.6, shaky and sweaty. What now?

options.text: Treat the low glucose now by the hospital hypoglycaemia protocol, recheck, and tell the senior and anaesthetist
Focus on the BP of 172/100 first
options.consequence: The glucose is the urgent problem.

decisions.prompt: He also takes an SGLT2 inhibitor. What now?

options.text: Ask when he last took it and check ketones; tell the anaesthetist
Ignore it because the glucose is low
options.consequence: Ketoacidosis can occur with a normal sugar.

decisions.prompt: HbA1c 76 and a hypoglycaemic event. What now?

options.text: The list is usually postponed; refer back to the diabetes team for optimisation
Proceed because the BP is below 180/110
options.consequence: Diabetes control is the reason to postpone.

correct: Do not chase the BP first

incorrect.mistake: Lets him go to theatre without checking ketones

debrief.if_ignored: Harm from the missed problem or an unsafe operation
debrief.remember: The most worrying-looking number is not always the most urgent one.

asa.why: Type 2 diabetes with a low glucose today and blood pressure 174/102: poorly controlled diabetes or blood pressure is ASA 3 in the book's list.
